schedules.title: Set up FLARE
schedules.description:
A schedule is the day's lighting: when each phase starts, and how bright and warm the light is. One schedule is enough for most homes, but each floor can have its own.

You can add or remove schedules later from FLARE's integration page.

schedule_names.title: Name your schedules
schedule_names.description: Add a name for each schedule you want. Each name becomes part of that schedule's entity IDs, so pick names you're happy to keep. If a schedule has the same name as a floor, that floor's areas start on it in the next step.

automations.title: Set up room automations?
automations.description:
FLARE can set up an automation for each area now, which drives the area's lights from its schedule.

Already have automations controlling your lights? Skip this for now, then move your rooms over one at a time with 'Set up area' on FLARE's integration page.

areas.title: Set up areas
areas.description:
Each area you set up gets a room automation from the FLARE blueprint, which drives its lights.

Pick the schedule each area follows, or clear it to leave that area out. You can set up more areas later with 'Set up area' on FLARE's integration page, and change which schedule a room follows in its automation.

flares.title: Add flares too?
flares.description:
A flare is a single light for a whole room, for voice assistants, HomeKit and dashboards. Turning it on switches the room on at its schedule's brightness and colour. Turning it on at a brightness or colour sets every light in the room to that, and FLARE leaves the room alone until it's empty and dark.

Skip this if you don't switch rooms that way. You can add flares later with 'Add flare' on FLARE's integration page.

flare_rooms.title: Pick rooms for flares
flare_rooms.description: Each room you pick gets a flare named after its area, and you can rename it afterwards.

user.title: Add schedule
user.description: A schedule is the day's lighting: when each phase starts, and how bright and warm the light is. It gets a device with this name, and its entity IDs start with the name, so "Living Room" gives sensor.living_room_flare. Its times and curve start at FLARE's defaults, and you can change them on the device's page or the FLARE Lighting dashboard.

reconfigure.title: Export or import this schedule
reconfigure.description: This is everything in this schedule: its times, brightness, colour temperatures and transitions. You can copy it to keep or share it. To replace this schedule, paste in another one and submit it. Anything you leave out keeps its current value.

error.already_configured: A schedule with that name already exists

user.title: Add flare
user.description:
A flare is a light for a whole room, to use from voice assistants, HomeKit or a dashboard. Turning it on runs the room's automation, so the room comes on the way it normally would.

If you turn it on with a brightness or colour, every light in the room is set to that, and turning it off turns every light in the room off. After either, FLARE leaves the room alone until it's empty and dark.

blueprint.title: Add flares for your rooms
blueprint.description: Each room you pick gets a flare named after its automation, in the automation's area, and you can rename it afterwards. Rooms that already have a flare aren't listed.

reload_for_dashboard.title: Reload to add FLARE's dashboard
reload_for_dashboard.description:
FLARE was set up while this page was open, and Home Assistant only loads an integration's dashboard when the page loads. {reload}, then find **FLARE Lighting** in Settings → Dashboards → Add dashboard.

If it still isn't listed, reload the page once more: your browser may show a saved copy of it first. This repair goes away once a browser has loaded FLARE's dashboard.

init.title: Settings
init.description:
**Two-step bulb models** lists the bulb models that need brightness and colour sent separately, one pattern per line. Each pattern is matched against a light's manufacturer and model, ignoring case, and * matches anything, as in *TRADFRI bulb* or IKEA*.

The field is pre-filled with FLARE's default patterns. Your saved list replaces those defaults entirely, so you can remove a pattern as well as add one, but it won't pick up patterns added in later releases. If you save the field empty, FLARE uses the defaults again.

Each area ticks once per **Update interval**, a gap apart from the next area, so rooms don't all send at once. A change smaller than the **Minimum brightness change** or **Minimum colour temperature change** isn't sent.

A light within the **Brightness tolerance for overrides** and the **Colour tolerance for overrides** of what FLARE asked for still counts as FLARE's, so only a change you'd notice reads as an override.

data_description.tick_interval: How often each area ticks, in minutes.
data_description.tick_gap: Seconds between one area's tick and the next. Shrinks automatically if the areas wouldn't otherwise fit in the interval.
data_description.min_brightness_change: A light within this percentage of its target brightness is left alone.
data_description.min_color_temp_change: A light within this many mireds of its target colour temperature is left alone.
data_description.override_brightness_tolerance: A light within this percentage of the brightness FLARE asked for still counts as FLARE's. Raise it if lights are marked overridden when nobody changed them.
data_description.override_color_temp_tolerance: A light within this many mireds of the colour temperature FLARE asked for still counts as FLARE's. Raise it if lights are marked overridden when nobody changed them.
